newsitem.title: POLAND: CARNEGIE RECOMMENDS TO BUY POLISH NFI 6 SHARES.
newsitem.headline: CARNEGIE RECOMMENDS TO BUY POLISH NFI 6 SHARES.

text.p: International investment bank Carnegie said investors should buy Polish National Investment Fund (NFI) 6, praising its strategy of concentrating on prospective sectors, Carnegie said in its January 7 report.

It said NFI 6 focused during the selection stage on the automotive, chemical and consumer goods industries, avoiding non-profitable sectors and those which would not be attractive for strategic investors.
"Magna Polonia represents an excellent opportunity to invest in a NFI that has demonstrated successful and proactive management with a well diversified and differentiated portfolio. Buy." it said.
NFI 6 is one of the 15 NFIs of the contry's mass privatisation programme in which about 500 companies are run by the NFIs. The funds are expected to enter the Warsaw bourse in the first half of 1997.
From November 1995 to November 1996, 25.7 million Poles bought mass privatisation certificates, to be later exchanged for shares in the NFIs.

Carnegie also stressed NFI 6 had good control over firms in its portfolio and said Chase Management Sp z o.o., which manages the fund had already successfully initiated the restructuring process in firms it runs.
According to unaudited results NFI 6 had a net loss of 34.6 million zlotys over the first nine months of 1996.
